camette.evidence: Michael W. Nolan 2002 Camette/Camelot-family game: board/setup diagram, soldier moves/canters/mandatory captures, royal charging, own-castle restriction, castle/all-capture/immobility wins. Readable complete text; original diagram remains online.

dablot-prejjesne.evidence: Dablot Prejjesne section and required preceding Alquerque rules. Specifically Mats Winther’s quoted interpretation: ranked king/prince/soldiers, forward soldier steps, short-leap captures, mandatory soldier captures, royal optional captures, king-capture or king-alone ending. These variant choices are explicit; not claimed as the unique traditional rules. Other unrelated Alquerque variants are excluded.

five-field-kono.evidence: Traditional Korean 5x5 seven-piece positional exchange: diagram setup, one-step diagonal moves, no capture, occupy opponent starting places. Deadlock commentary and a proposed optional tuning rule are separately labelled and are not adopted as base rules.

gothic-checkers.evidence: Traditional German Altdeutsche Dame: 8x8 setup, forward-diagonal soldiers and five-direction mandatory maximum captures, promotion, king movement/capture and elimination. Source explicitly discusses uncertainty/reconstruction and competing historical king ranges; do not treat one version as universal.

jeson-mor.evidence: Mongolian nine-horse game: 9x9 setup diagram, chess-knight moves/captures, occupy-and-leave center or capture all opposing horses. Short complete rules plus example.

sanqi.evidence: L. Lynn Smith 2003 SanQi: initially empty hex board, three neutral colors, placement or neighborhood-majority recoloring, one-turn ko, first-player circle/second-player line and either-player triangle goals, with author strategy/examples.

rise.evidence: Complete correct two-page 2012 illustrated manual reviewed; earlier dlp 2022 article rejected.

apocalypse.evidence: Correct simultaneous variant in attributed Wikipedia connected-reader snapshot; current Neto adaptation excluded.

quod.evidence: Matching complete implementation rules section; original raw Git blob hash independently checked.

leap-frog.reason: 1939 eight-frog non-capturing race, 2000 Huntoon capture/stalemate game and stored pre-1898 multi-player solitaire are distinct. Local summary conflates racing/capture and says four frogs. No uniquely matched target established.

followup.evidence: The previously held alternatives remain rejected. Walker’s complete 2011 Leaflet 30 explicitly matches the pre-1898 and Murray-1898 shared-piece capture/scoring game. It is distinct from the 1939 race and 2000 Huntoon game. The local summary combines incompatible variants and does not coherently identify a different named game. BGG35722 is retained with source scope explicit; the source is accepted and specific fundamental errors are recorded.

3-6-9.reason: Named description is a 52-card trick-taking game; stored primary and Neto match are Townsend’s 9x9 single-color placement/line-score abstract. Do not accept board rules for the described card game.
